🚨 GEMINI 4 IS NOW SHOWING UP IN ARENA.

And the first side-by-side with GPT-6 is already interesting.

Same prompt.
Same goal.
Two frontier models.
Gemini 4's result looks seriously impressive, especially in the way it handles the build and overall execution.
GPT-6 still holds its own, but the gap may be getting a lot smaller than people expected.

If Gemini 4 can consistently match GPT-6 across different tasks, Google may have just entered the next phase of the AI model war.

This is only one comparison.

More tests needed.

post.originalText:
🚨 GEMINI 4 PRO SURPRISES AGAIN, AND THIS TIME IT'S A MECHANICAL BUTTERFLY

Prompt was simple: build a beautiful mechanical butterfly in Three.js.

What came back isn't a static render. It's a full interactive engineering study, "Papilio Mechanica," brass and blued steel wings built from real mechanical gear clusters, an assembled/exploded toggle, material swaps between azure, gold and obsidian finishes, and hover tooltips that explain individual components.

Spec sheet included: 6.2m wingspan, 2.4kg mass, 112° stroke, 2.3Hz beat rate. Orbit, zoom, pan, take flight, all built into the scene itself.

This is the same checkpoint pattern we've been tracking, an unlabeled model producing outputs well above what its listed tier should be capable of.

Worth being precise here rather than just repeating the claim: the mystery checkpoint people have been catching in Arena has been showing up under the "gemini-3.8-flash" label specifically, not 3.7. Gemini 3.7 Flash is a fully public, already documented GA model with its own model card and benchmarks, so if a source says 3.7, that's worth double checking before repeating it.

Either way, the actual output here speaks for itself regardless of which label it was hiding under.
